title: Choose the PromoterLab visual world
question: A redesigned PromoterLab needs one durable visual language. The recommended direction makes sequence analysis feel like live evidence under a UV transilluminator; the alternatives are different, equally complete interpretations. Keep the roll, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: UV Field Notebook
options.lineage: A working molecular-biology notebook observed beneath a blue-light transilluminator
options.body: Deep ultraviolet navy becomes the laboratory field; luminous electrophoresis bands, annotation ticks, and exact sequence fragments carry the interface. The first viewport pairs a live sequence ribbon with an honest ‘Explore sequence’ action. The workbench becomes a calm analysis bench, not a generic SaaS dashboard. Risk: its dark scientific atmosphere must retain strong text contrast and never make results feel decorative.

options.label: Riso Lab Atlas
options.lineage: A spot-ink scientific atlas with misregistered layers
options.body: A tactile public-facing science publication: fluorescent spot layers distinguish motifs and models; responsive panels retain clear UI behavior. It makes learning content memorable, but is less naturally suited to the authenticated research console.

options.label: Signal Instrument
options.lineage: A precision instrument panel with physical measurement grammar
options.body: A focused operational world of calibrated scales and live signal traces, ideal for the classifier and history views. It communicates rigor immediately, though it makes the public learning surface less expressive.
